title: Word equations practice sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 9 (Word equations practice sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 9: Burning fuels. To understand combustion as a reaction between a fuel and oxygen that releases energy

model.title: Write a word equation for burning methane

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Products of a hydrocarbon: carbon dioxide + water

questions.q: Write the word equation for propane burning completely.
questions.model: Reactants: the fuel (propane) and oxygen. Products of any hydrocarbon burning completely: carbon dioxide and water. So propane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.

questions.q: How do we test for water?
questions.a: Blue cobalt chloride paper turns pink (or white anhydrous copper sulfate turns blue).

questions.q: Core: Write word equations for burning methane, butane and hydrogen.
questions.a: methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water; butane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water; hydrogen + oxygen → water.
questions.model: Teacher writes methane first: methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Hydrocarbon in, carbon dioxide and water out.

questions.q: Extend: Why does hydrogen make no carbon dioxide when it burns?
Stretch: A candle on a balance loses mass as it burns. Explain why this does not break the law of conservation of mass. Write in the portal response box.
questions.a: The products (carbon dioxide and water vapour) escape as gases; if collected, the total mass of products would equal the wax and oxygen used.

questions.q: The products of complete combustion of a hydrocarbon are...
Big question: where does a candle go when it burns?
questions.a: The wax reacts with oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water vapour, which escape into the air.
